docs.text: Getting started ¶ BLUF: Three commands take you from nothing to a book: install, check, write. The install is one line, the check tells you every gap with its fix, and the book is written by a free model on your own machine. The full stack (an API, a queue and a worker) is a separate, optional step at the end. curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence/main/install.sh | sh ei doctor --ready ei book create --kind nonfiction "how to keep herbs alive indoors" --budget-usd 5 \ --out ./my-book --profile ~/.config/engineering-influence/author.toml Before you type anything ¶ Daniel: The install line pipes a script from the internet straight into my shell. My last job would have walked me out of the building for that. Professor Feynman: Good instinct. What exactly are you afraid of? Daniel: That I do not know what it does until it has done it. Professor Feynman: Then make it tell you first. Add --dry-run . It prints every command it would run and changes nothing. It is the difference between a mover carrying your piano upstairs and a mover walking the route with you and pointing at each doorway. Daniel: So I read the list, and if I dislike a doorway? Professor Feynman: Skip it. --skip-model leaves Ollama alone, --skip-tex leaves TeX alone, --skip-search starts no search. Or read the script itself: it is one file, with what it does written at the top. The walk-through has a limit, mind you. It shows the commands, not what those commands download. Daniel: And afterwards, how do I know it worked? Professor Feynman: You do not take its word. You ask a second question: ei doctor --ready . One line per thing a book needs, ok or FAIL , and every FAIL says what to do. Tell me what you would run first. Daniel: The dry run. Then the real one. Then the doctor, and I do not start a book while it says FAIL . 1. Install ¶ You need macOS with Homebrew , or Linux with apt-get . See what it will do first: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --dry-run Then run it: curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence/main/install.sh | sh Step What it installs Size Skip with 1 uv if missing, then ei with the runtime , publishing and mcp extras small 2 Ollama and the model gpt-oss:20b about 13 GB --skip-model 3 The TeX tools that build the PDF and the EPUB several GB --skip-tex 4 A local SearXNG for the research stage, if Docker with compose is present a container --skip-search 5 A starter author profile at ~/.config/engineering-influence/author.toml a file never written over 6 Runs ei doctor --ready and prints the command that writes a book Other options: --with-claude-skill puts the Claude Code skill in ~/.claude/skills/ , and --version REF installs a tag, branch or commit instead of main . Options go after sh -s -- , because the script itself is arriving on standard input. The script asks no questions, because a piped script has no keyboard. A step that needs administrator rights runs sudo , which asks for your password itself. Run it twice and the second run changes nothing already in place. What is not verified: the script has been run for real only as a dry run on macOS. The Linux path is tested against stand-in tools. On Linux it prints how to set Ollama's context size and does not set it. On a Mac without Homebrew it stops and tells you to install Homebrew. It installs from main , which gets the script with the next release. By hand instead: uv tool install "engineering-influence[runtime,publishing,mcp] @ git+https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence" , then the tools in WORKER_IMAGE.md and the model in LOCAL_MODEL.md . 2. Check the machine ¶ ei doctor --ready ok install: extra runtime: installed ok install: tool lualatex: /Library/TeX/texbin/lualatex FAIL install: author profile: none named: set EI_AUTHOR_PROFILE or pass --author-profile FILE (…) ok local: model: gpt-oss:20b is pulled ok local: context: 131072 tokens, at least the 32768 a prompt is assembled to fit … 1 of 14 checks failed It checks Why it matters The runtime and publishing extras Without them a run stops at once lualatex , latexmk , tex4ebook , zip , and pdftoppm or mutool Without them every chapter is written and then the last stage, build , fails epubcheck (optional) Only a strict release needs it; without it the EPUB gets the built-in checks The author profile A book cannot be typeset without the author's name, imprint and bio The local model: the server, the model, one tiny answer, the context size It is what writes the book The search The research stage needs one It exits 0 when everything passed, 1 when a check failed and 2 on setup trouble. It sends one tiny completion to the local model, which stays on your machine, and one search request to each search you have configured. 3. Fill in your author profile ¶ Open ~/.config/engineering-influence/author.toml and replace every value with your own. It is the title page, the copyright page and the about-the-author page. It is never sent to a model. author = "Your Name" publisher = "Your Imprint" edition = "First Edition" author_bio = "One or two sentences about you, as you want them printed in the book." The other keys, and the [pricing] table a strict release needs, are in CONFIGURATION.md . 4. Write a book ¶ ei book create --kind nonfiction "how to keep herbs alive indoors" --budget-usd 5 \ --out ./my-book --profile ~/.config/engineering-influence/author.toml It prints an estimate, then one line per stage as each finishes, then a summary. --kind novel writes a novel. --out must be a new or empty folder. --budget-usd is required even with the free model, where it is only a cap. A whole book takes a long time; how long on your machine is not yet measured. Exit Meaning What to do 0 The book is written Open my-book/run/book/ and read my-book/run/quality-report.json 1 The run failed, and a failed run is final; what it made is still in my-book/ Read the issue: lines it printed, fix the cause, and start a new run with a new --out 2 It could not start The message says why 3 It stopped to ask for more budget; nothing is lost ei book create --out ./my-book --resume --approve-spend If it is interrupted (a crash, a closed laptop, a provider that was out of capacity), carry on: ei book create --out ./my-book --resume Finished stages are never run or paid for again. The run is kept in my-book.state/ . A run that ended in failure (exit 1) is final: --resume returns it as it is and does not try again. A failed run's chapters are still in my-book/ . What is in the folder, and every flag: INTERACTIONS.md and BOOKS_AND_KDP.md . Run the stack ¶ Everything above is one process and needs no server. The stack is for many runs, other machines and other programs: a REST API, a queue, a worker, the SDK, the MCP server and webhooks. You need a clone of the repository, Docker with compose, uv and python3 . git clone https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence cd engineering-influence sh examples/up.sh set -a; . examples/.env; set +a curl -fsS "$EI_BASE_URL/health/ready" # {"status":"ready"} uv run examples/api/start_pipeline.py The first run writes examples/.env (git-ignored, mode 600) with random database and broker passwords and one API key, then builds the image and starts five services: Postgres, RabbitMQ, a one-shot database migration, the API on 127.0.0.1:8000 and the worker. It waits until every container is healthy. Nothing has a default credential, and nothing is reachable from your network. ready: 200 ready without a key: 401 started: 200 {"job_id": "6c05b79f-…", "project_slug": "sample-essay"} This demo proves the plumbing, not the writing. The example worker runs EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR=deterministic , which writes placeholder text, and start_pipeline is the older stage pipeline. To write real books on the stack, give the worker a model and the TeX image: WORKER_IMAGE.md and CONFIGURATION.md . Interface Command Reference curl sh examples/api/run.sh REST SDK (sync) uv run python examples/sdk/sync_client.py SDK SDK (async) uv run python examples/sdk/async_client.py SDK MCP uv run python examples/mcp/client.py MCP CLI EI="uv run ei" sh examples/cli/run.sh CLI Observability uv run examples/observability/scrape.py Operations Webhooks see examples/README.md Webhooks Watch the worker: docker compose -f examples/docker-compose.yml --env-file examples/.env logs -f worker . Stop with sh examples/down.sh (keep the data) or sh examples/down.sh --volumes (delete it). Work on the code ¶ git clone https://github.com/adammatthewsteinberger/engineering-influence cd engineering-influence uv sync --extra test --extra runtime --extra api --extra dev --extra publishing uv run ei --version # engineering-influence 0.1.0a2 The gates a change must pass are in CONTRIBUTING.md and TESTING.md . Where to go next ¶ Let an AI agent run it for you: AGENTS_DRIVING.md . Something went wrong: TROUBLESHOOTING.md . Every variable and what fails closed: CONFIGURATION.md . How it is built: ARCHITECTURE.md .

Nothing has a default credential, and nothing is reachable from your network. ready: 200 ready without a key: 401 started: 200 {"job_id": "6c05b79f-…", "project_slug": "sample-essay"} This demo proves the plumbing, not the writing. The example worker runs EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR=deterministic , which writes placeholder text, and start_pipeline is the older stage pipeline. To write real books on the stack, give the worker a model and the TeX image: WORKER_IMAGE.md and CONFIGURATION.md . Interface Command Reference curl sh examples/api/run.sh REST SDK (sync) uv run python examples/sdk/sync_client.py SDK SDK (async) uv run python examples/sdk/async_client.py SDK MCP uv run python examples/mcp/client.py MCP CLI EI="uv run ei" sh examples/cli/run.sh CLI Observability uv run examples/observability/scrape.py Operations Webhooks see examples/README.md Webhooks Watch the worker: docker compose -f examples/docker-compose.yml --env-file examples/.env logs -f worker . Stop with sh examples/down.sh (keep the data) or sh examples/down.sh --volumes (delete it).

docs.text: Interfaces reference ¶ BLUF: Every interface drives the same thing, a book run that ends in a KDP-ready package, so learn one and you know them all. To write one book, use the CLI ( ei book create ). To serve many, run the stack and call it over REST, the SDK, MCP or the Agent Client Protocol. This page is the contract for each: requests, replies, flags, exit codes and the error codes a caller meets most. Every interface starts or drives the same thing: an autonomous book-writing run that ends in a KDP-ready package ( details ). Six interfaces sit over the same controller layer, so they accept the same request and return the same result. Pick by who is calling. Interface Process Authenticated Reaches the stack REST API ei serve api API key yes Python SDK your code API key yes (it calls the REST API) MCP server stdio child process no (local only) yes with ei serve mcp ; the example server is in-memory CLI ei no (local only) serve , run and book yes; pipeline start no Agent Client Protocol ei acp (stdio) no (local only) yes Webhooks outbound HTTPS HMAC signature yes One counter, several windows ¶ Daniel: Six ways in. REST, an SDK, MCP, a CLI, ACP, webhooks. Do I have to learn six products? Professor Feynman: Think of a bank. You can walk to the counter, use the machine outside, or phone. How many banks is that? Daniel: One. The same account, the same rules, whichever way I ask. Professor Feynman: Same here. Each interface is a window; behind all of them is one counter, the controller layer. A window translates your request and hands it over. The rules about runs and money live behind the counter. A window may be stricter, never looser: the MCP window caps a run at five dollars and cannot grant more budget unless you allow it. Daniel: So if the API refuses a budget above the operator's limit, the MCP tool refuses it too. Professor Feynman: For the same reason, though not in the same words. REST gives you a code, BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT . MCP and ACP give you the message. Now the limit of the picture: not every window is open to the street. The REST API checks a key. The CLI, the MCP server and ACP check nothing, because they are meant to run on your own machine, so they must never be put on a network. Daniel: Then I pick the window by who is calling, and I read one set of rules. I will start at the table below. The request ¶ Every start request is a project : Field Type Rules slug string required, at least 1 character title string required, at least 1 character postulates list of strings required, at least 1: the claims the pipeline must stay within stages list of strings required, at least 1, from thesis , book , novel , screenplay , hub , spokes , distribution , publish The result is {"job_id": "<id>", "project_slug": "<slug>"} : the job queued for the first stage. The worker runs the stages in the order given. A book run starts from a brief instead ( POST /v1/runs , ei run create , the SDK and MCP create_run , and ei book create , which builds one from its flags). Any key not in this table is refused: Field Rules schema_version 1 , the default kind required: nonfiction or novel idea required, not blank budget_micro_usd required: a whole number above 0, in millionths of a dollar title_hint , audience optional, not blank target_words optional, above 0 trim_size optional: 5x8 , 5.5x8.5 or 6x9 language default en inputs at most 8 of {name, text, origin} ; origin is pasted (the default) or file ; names unique; 200,000 characters in all violence novels only: none , mild , moderate or graphic heat novels only: none , sweet , steamy or explicit REST API ¶ Run it with ei serve api (see CONFIGURATION.md ); the compose stack publishes it on 127.0.0.1:8000 . Method and path Auth Purpose POST /v1/pipelines key Start a pipeline. Body: a project. 200 with the result. GET /v1/runs key Every saved run, as run summaries (the artifact list is empty here; GET /v1/runs/{run_id} lists a run's artifacts). 200 . Present only when the API is wired with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/resume key Un-park a parked run and queue its current stage. 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 finished. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel key Stop a run for good. 200 with the run; 404 unknown. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/grant key Give a run more budget and continue it. Body {"micro_usd": N} or none: a run waiting for consent gets exactly the amount it asked for (a different amount is 409 ); a parked run needs micro_usd . 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 not waiting or parked, or changed meanwhile. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/deny key Refuse a run's request for more budget; the run parks and nothing is queued. 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 not waiting for consent. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs key Start a book run from a brief (the brief contract v1, the same body ei run create reads as TOML). 201 with the new run, pending at its first stage; 422 when the body is not a brief or the kind is not one this build can start. Present only when the API is wired with run creation. GET /v1/runs/{run_id} key A book run: status, stage, plan, budget in micro-dollars, issues and the names of its artifacts. 200 with a RunSummaryV1 . GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/artifacts/{name} key One stored artifact, byte for byte, as application/octet-stream with nosniff and no-store . Names may contain / . GET /health/live none {"status":"alive"} while the process runs. GET /health/ready none 200 {"status":"ready"} or 503 {"status":"unavailable"} . GET /metrics key Prometheus text format. GET /docs , /openapi.json none FastAPI's generated schema for this build. Authentication. Send Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-API-Key: <key> . Keys come from EI_API_KEYS . There is no unauthenticated mode. Correlation. Send X-Request-ID (8 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - ) or a W3C traceparent ; otherwise one is generated. It is echoed in the X-Request-ID response header, copied into the queued job, restored by the worker and sent on outbound webhooks. Errors. Application errors are {"code", "message", "retryable"} : Status code Meaning Retry? 401 UNAUTHORIZED Missing or wrong key no 429 RATE_LIMITED Per-address or per-key budget spent yes, with backoff 404 RUN_NOT_FOUND No run has that id no 404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND The run has no such artifact; a name that could never be stored (absolute, .. , backslash) gets the same answer no 422 n/a Body failed validation (FastAPI's detail list) no, fix the body 409 RUN_FINISHED The run is completed, failed or cancelled, so it cannot be resumed or cancelled no 409 RUN_CHANGED The run changed while it was being answered yes 409 CONSENT_NOT_PENDING A grant or a denial for a run that is not waiting for one no 422 BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT The budget asked for is above the operator's limit for one run no, ask for less 422 OUTSTANDING_BUDGET_EXCEEDED All unfinished runs together would hold more unspent budget than the operator allows later, when runs finish 422 RUN_KIND_UNSUPPORTED This build cannot start that kind of book no 503 SECRET_MISSING A required secret is not configured after fixing configuration These are the codes a caller of the API meets most. Every code the package can raise is frozen in tests/contracts/snapshots/error_codes.json ; most of the rest stop a process at start and are described beside the setting they concern in CONFIGURATION.md . Python with requests : import os, requests base, key = os.environ["EI_BASE_URL"], os.environ["EI_API_KEY"] reply = requests.post( f"{base}/v1/pipelines", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, json={ "slug": "sample-essay", "title": "A Sample Essay", "postulates": ["Claims must be supported by evidence."], "stages": ["thesis"], }, timeout=10, ) reply.raise_for_status() print(reply.json()) # {'job_id': '…', 'project_slug': 'sample-essay'} Full scripts: examples/api/start_pipeline.py , examples/api/run.sh . Python SDK ¶ packages/engineering-influence-sdk is a thin typed wrapper over httpx for the operations the API has: starting a pipeline, creating a book run from a brief ( create_run ), and listing, resuming and cancelling runs ( list_runs , resume_run , cancel_run ), answering a run's request for more budget ( grant_run , deny_run ), and reading a run ( get_run ) and the files it stored ( get_artifact , as bytes). It ships in this repository and in each release. from engineering_influence_sdk import EngineeringInfluenceClient client = EngineeringInfluenceClient("http://127.0.0.1:8000", api_key) started = client.start_pipeline( "sample-essay", "A Sample Essay", ("Claims must be supported by evidence.",), ("thesis", "book") ) run = client.create_run( { "schema_version": 1, "kind": "nonfiction", "idea": "Windowsill herbs", "budget_micro_usd": 5000000, } ) status = client.get_run(run["run_id"]) # status, stage, budget and the names of its artifacts pdf = client.get_artifact(run["run_id"], "book/my-book.pdf") # bytes, once the run has built it client.close() AsyncEngineeringInfluenceClient has the same signature with await (and await client.close() ). Any non-2xx answer raises httpx.HTTPStatusError ; the API's error document is in error.response . Scripts: examples/sdk/ . MCP server ¶ ei serve mcp runs the stack's MCP server over stdio, for an MCP host (Claude Desktop, an agent runtime) to start as a child process. It needs EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL like the API (and a migrated database: ei db upgrade ), offers the same runs the REST API does, and needs no API key because the host that starts it already holds the stack's credentials. Standard output carries the protocol, so logs (JSON) go to standard error only. A host entry looks like: {"mcpServers": {"engineering-influence": {"command": "ei", "args": ["serve", "mcp"], "env": {"EI_DATABASE_URL": "postgresql+psycopg://...", "EI_RABBITMQ_URL": "amqp://..."}}}} The server does not offer grant_run or deny_run unless the operator sets EI_MCP_ALLOW_SPEND=1 . Granting a run budget is the person's decision, and an agent that could raise its own run's cap would have no cap. Without the setting an agent can start a run, watch it, resume or cancel it and read what it made; a run that needs more budget shows as awaiting_consent in get_run , and the person answers it with ei run grant . A run an agent starts is held to EI_MCP_MAX_RUN_BUDGET_MICRO_USD (default 5,000,000, five dollars): create_run refuses a brief with a bigger budget_micro_usd ( BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT ), so an agent cannot open a run with a cap of its own choosing. That bounds one run, not how many runs an agent starts . For that, set the stack-wide ceilings below ( EI_MAX_OUTSTANDING_BUDGET_MICRO_USD ), which hold every way into the stack, MCP included. McpApplication(controller).build() returns an MCPServer (from the official mcp 2.x SDK) with one tool when built bare, and the rest when it is given the services ( grant_run and deny_run only with allow_spend=True ): Tool Arguments Returns start_pipeline slug , title , postulates (list), stages (list) {"job_id", "project_slug"} list_runs none every saved run as run summaries (present only with run management) resume_run run_id the run after un-parking it (present only with run management) cancel_run run_id the run after cancelling it (present only with run management) get_run run_id a run's RunSummaryV1 : status, stage, budget and the names of its stored artifacts (present only when the server is built with a run reader) read_artifact run_id , name (such as book/my-book.pdf ) {name, bytes, encoding, content} : the text when the file is UTF-8, base64 when it is not. A file over 1 MiB is refused ( ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE ) and the message names the GET /v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name} address that downloads any size (present with get_run ) create_run brief (an object: the brief contract v1) the new run as a RunSummaryV1 , pending at its first stage. Present only when the server is built with a run creator grant_run run_id , optional micro_usd the run after allowing it more budget. Present only with allow_spend=True ( ei serve mcp sets it from EI_MCP_ALLOW_SPEND ) deny_run run_id the run after refusing it more budget; it parks. Present only with allow_spend=True examples/mcp/server.py is the bare server over in-memory adapters, for trying the tool shapes without a stack, and examples/mcp/client.py is a client that spawns it, lists the tools and calls one. The server is a local process: it is not authenticated, so do not expose it on a network. In-memory only: it does not queue work on the stack. --stage defaults to thesis . 0 ; 2 on a usage error ei serve api / worker / mcp Runs the API, the worker or the stdio MCP server from EI_* settings (see MCP server ). 0 on a clean stop; 1 an extra is missing (the message names which); 2 and one line naming the bad variable; never a traceback ei doctor Checks that this installation is ready, never asking a paid model to answer. --ready answers whether this machine can make a book now : the extras, the tools the build stage calls, the author profile ( --author-profile FILE , else EI_AUTHOR_PROFILE ), then the local model and the search, every check made and printed in one run. The others check one thing: --models the model profiles and catalog ( --probe adds one model-list request per profile), --search one real search through each configured provider, --local the free local model. See MODEL_PROFILES.md and LOCAL_MODEL.md . 0 ready; 1 a check failed; 2 setup trouble ei db upgrade Applies the database migrations to EI_DATABASE_URL and prints the revision reached. Needs the runtime extra. 0 ; 1 extra missing; 2 and one line for a missing setting or an unreachable database ei run status RUN_ID Prints the run as one line of JSON (the same RunSummaryV1 the API returns). Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . 0 ; 1 unknown run, or the runtime extra is missing (true of every ei run command); 2 setup trouble ei run create BRIEF.TOML Starts a book run from a brief file (TOML, the brief contract v1: kind , idea , budget_micro_usd and the optional keys). The run is saved pending with the brief's cap as its budget and its first stage is queued for the worker; a file that is not a brief, or a kind this build cannot start, is refused on one line and nothing is saved. Needs the database and the broker, like resume . 0 ; 1 a file that cannot be read or is not a brief, or a kind this build cannot start; 2 setup trouble, or a budget an operator ceiling refuses ei run runs Lists every saved run, one line each: its id, status and current stage. Needs only the database. 0 ; 2 setup trouble ei run resume RUN_ID Moves a parked run back to running and queues its current stage; on a run that is already running it only queues the stage again, which repairs a resume that died half-way. Reads EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL . 0 ; 1 unknown run, finished run or a run that kept changing; 2 setup trouble ei run cancel RUN_ID Stops a run for good; cancelling twice is fine, and a completed or failed run is refused. Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . same ei run grant RUN_ID [--micro-usd N] Gives a run more budget and continues it. A run waiting for consent gets exactly the amount it asked for (passing another amount is refused); a parked run needs --micro-usd and gets exactly that. The stage is queued. Needs EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL . 0 ; 1 the run is not waiting for consent or parked, or it changed while being answered; 2 setup trouble, or a grant an operator ceiling refuses ei run deny RUN_ID Refuses a run's request for more budget. The run parks, and nothing is queued; it can be granted more later. Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . same ei run export RUN_ID DIRECTORY Writes what a run produced to a new or empty folder: the book as a project at the top ( books/<slug>.toml and src/chapter_NN.md , as the book commands expect) and every other artifact under run/ (the stage outputs and the audit/ reports). It reads the run and changes nothing in it. Nothing is overwritten, and either every file is written or none is. A folder that holds anything is refused, as is a run that has stored nothing. Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . 0 ; 1 unknown run, a run with nothing stored, or a folder that is not empty; 2 setup trouble ei book create --kind KIND IDEA --budget-usd N --out DIR --profile FILE Makes a whole book from an idea, in this process, with nobody in the loop. It runs every stage of the plan for the kind (brief to build; see BOOKS_AND_KDP.md ) with the models and search the environment names ( EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR and its settings, as for a worker), then writes the book to --out (a new or empty folder): the project at the top ( books/ , src/ ) and every artifact under run/ , so the finished PDF, EPUB, covers, listing and manifest are in run/book/ , the readiness reports in run/build/ , and run/quality-report.json says how it came out. --budget-usd has no default, and --profile (or EI_AUTHOR_PROFILE ) is required, because the author's details are needed to typeset the book: both are checked before anything is spent . Before anything is spent it says what the book is expected to cost with the priced model ( estimate: about 6.00 USD for the whole book (4.00 before editing), against a budget of 5.00: tight ) and grades the budget: short (below what the essential stages are expected to cost: refused, with the budget that would do, unless --ignore-estimate ), tight (may stop to ask for more), lean (an editing pass that runs out of money is skipped) or ample . With the free local model the estimate is still printed, from a price of zero; with the offline placeholder there is no estimate. Optional: --title , --audience , --target-words , --trim-size , --ignore-estimate , and --strict-release (fails the build on any release warning; needs [pricing] in the profile). The run is kept in a SQLite file in OUT.state/ ( --state-dir to move it), so a process that dies loses nothing that was paid for: --resume continues it, and a model call already made is replayed, not paid for again. When the run asks for more budget it stops and writes nothing; --resume --approve-spend grants exactly what it asked for. A failed run is final, but what it made is still written to --out . 0 the book is written; 1 the run failed or a needed extra is missing; 2 the command could not start (a missing idea, kind, budget or profile, a bad profile, a folder that already holds a run, or a budget below the estimate without --ignore-estimate ); 3 the run stopped to ask for budget, or parked because the provider is at capacity ei book … Audit, build and publish books (needs the publishing extra and, for PDFs, a TeX toolchain). With no SLUG a subcommand works on every configured book. --dpi defaults to 90, and below 36 is refused (exit 2 ). package SLUG writes the KDP release bundle ( build/SLUG/release/kdp , see BOOKS_AND_KDP.md ) and refuses a failing release. Reads engineering-influence.toml in --root . 0 ok; 1 a build or audit failure; 2 bad arguments ei evaluate --out DIR --budget-usd N --judge-budget-usd N Spends real money. Makes every book of the evaluation set ( evaluation/set.toml ) with the stack's own pipeline, has the judge model ( EI_EVAL_JUDGE_PROFILE ) score each finished book on the rubric ( evaluation/rubric.toml ), and checks the release against the 1.0 bar: every book finished, every dimension's mean at least 3.5, none fallen by more than 0.2 from --baseline , and the cost estimate within 30% of what was spent. Refuses to start unless EI_ALLOW_PAID=1 . --budget-usd is the most each book may spend and --judge-budget-usd the most the judge may spend in all; neither has a default. --out must be a new or empty folder; evaluation.json is written there beside the books, and is the next release's baseline. See EVALUATION.md . 0 the release meets the bar; 1 it does not (each reason is printed) or a needed extra is missing; 2 the command could not run (not paid for, a bad budget, a folder that is not empty, a bad rubric or set, no judge named, or a judge that failed) ei tools add NAME -- COMMAND … Runs an MCP server once, under limits and with a bare environment, and records what it is in the tool lock: its files' hashes, the name and version it reported and a hash of its tools. Options go before NAME . Refuses a launcher ( npx , uvx , docker , …) and a relative script path before anything is run. See TOOL_LOCK.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools add --url URL NAME Contacts a remote MCP server once and records its address, the name and version it reported and a hash of its tools. Only https to a public address is allowed; the token, if any, is the variable named by --bearer-env . The server's code is not locked, only what it advertises. See TOOL_LOCK.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools list Shows the locked servers. Starts nothing. 0 ; 2 an unusable lock ei tools verify [NAME …] Runs each locked server (a server whose files changed is not started) and compares it with the lock. 0 all match; 1 one does not; 2 setup trouble or an unknown name ei tools grant NAME STAGE TOOL … Lets a stage call some of a locked server's tools: edits the lock, runs nothing. The tools must be ones the lock lists; no wildcards. A stage with no grant gets none. 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools revoke NAME STAGE [TOOL …] Takes tools back from a stage, or all of them if none are named. A stage with no grant is an error. same ei skills add FILE Reads a skill file once, checks it strictly (no key but name , version , description and [parts] ; no invisible or control characters) and records the SHA-256 of its bytes in the skill lock, keeping a copy in skills/ beside it. Enables nothing ; prints each part so you can read what will be added to prompts. --replace locks it again and clears its stages. Starts nothing. See SKILLS.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei skills import SOURCE … Turns a SKILL.md (a --- block of key: value lines, then markdown) into a skill file ( --out ) and prints what it kept and set aside, to be reviewed and then added. It does not touch the lock. See SKILLS.md . 0 ; 2 an unreadable source or a bad option ei skills enable NAME STAGE Lets a stage's prompt carry a skill: checks the file against its hash and refuses a stage the skill has no text for. At most four skills per stage. same ei skills disable NAME STAGE Stops a stage carrying a skill. same ei skills remove NAME Unlocks a skill and deletes its copy. same ei skills list Shows the locked skills with their short hash and stages. Reads no skill file. 0 ; 2 an unusable lock ei skills verify Re-hashes every locked skill, enabled or not, against the lock. 0 all match; 1 one does not; 2 setup trouble ei plugins show FILE Reads a plugin file and says what installing it would do: its skills (with their text), and the ei tools add command for each server. Changes nothing. See PLUGINS.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal ei plugins import FOLDER Turns a plugin folder written for Claude Code into a bundle file ( --out ), to be shown and then added. It does not touch the lock. See PLUGINS.md . 0 ; 2 an unreadable folder or a bad option ei plugins add FILE Locks the bundle's skills (each enabled for no stage), keeps a copy of the bundle, and records its SHA-256 in the plugin lock. Starts nothing, contacts nothing, grants nothing: the commands for its servers are printed for you to review and run. Refuses a plugin that is installed or skills that are already locked, before writing anything. 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei plugins list Shows the installed plugins, the skills installed and the servers described. 0 ; 2 an unusable lock ei plugins verify Re-hashes each kept bundle and checks that its skills are still locked as installed. 0 all match; 1 one does not; 2 setup trouble ei plugins remove NAME Uninstalls a plugin and the skills it installed that are still exactly what it installed; a skill locked again since is left. 0 ; 2 on a refusal ei plugins search INDEX [TEXT] Lists the plugins in a marketplace index (a file on disk or an https:// address), or those whose name or description has the text. May use a network for an https:// index; installs nothing. See PLUGINS.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal ei plugins fetch INDEX NAME [--output DIR] Downloads one plugin file from an index, checks its SHA-256 against the index's before reading it , checks it is the plugin and version listed, and saves it as NAME.toml (never over an existing file). Installs nothing: it prints the show and add commands to run next. 0 ; 2 on a refusal, a hash that differs or a download that fails ei acp Serves the Agent Client Protocol (stable, version 1) over stdin and stdout, for an editor or agent client. Each line is one JSON-RPC message; only protocol messages go to stdout, and logs and errors go to stderr. Needs the runtime extra and EI_DATABASE_URL . See Agent Client Protocol . 0 when the input ends; 1 the runtime extra is missing; 2 setup trouble python -m engineering_influence is the same program. Walk-through: examples/cli/run.sh . Agent Client Protocol ¶ ei acp speaks the Agent Client Protocol, version 1 of the stable specification, so an editor or agent client can start book runs the way ei run create does. Only the parts below are implemented; anything else is refused with ACP_METHOD_NOT_FOUND . initialize agrees version 1, reports loadSession: true and no authentication methods. session/load takes a sessionId this agent stored, and an absolute cwd . It re-attaches the session, so a client can reconnect to a new ei acp process. It sends one session/update notice with the run's current state (if the session has a run), then replies with no result. A run that has finished is replayed but not followed. session/new takes an absolute cwd and returns a sessionId . mcpServers must be empty: this agent does not connect MCP servers yet. session/prompt takes text content blocks, joined by newlines and read as a brief in TOML, the same contract ei run create reads. The first prompt of a session starts its run, a second prompt in the same session is refused, and the turn ends with stopReason: end_turn once the run is saved and its first stage queued. The stages themselves run in the worker, not in the session. Before the turn ends the agent sends one session/update notice naming the run and its stage. session/cancel is a notification. It stops the session's run and gets no reply. Sessions are stored in the database beside the runs, so any ei acp process can load one. A run outlives its session, so ei run status RUN_ID and ei run cancel RUN_ID still work after the client disconnects. The session store needs migration 0002 : run ei db upgrade first. While a session is open, the agent follows its run. Every second it reads the run's saved state, and it sends a session/update notice when the status or the stage changes, once per change. A finished run (completed, failed or cancelled) is reported once and then no longer followed; a parked run is still followed, because it can be resumed. A notice is written between replies and never inside one. A failed read is one line on stderr, and the following goes on. A run that would spend past its cap does not fail: its next model call is refused before it spends, and the run stops in awaiting_consent with the amount the call needs. An open session is asked, with a session/request_permission request that offers grant (allow exactly that amount) and deny (the run parks). The answer decides the run; a cancelled answer leaves it waiting. The same decision is available from the command line with ei run grant and ei run deny for any run, including one with no open session. A parked run waiting for no decision continues with ei run grant RUN_ID --micro-usd N . Not yet implemented: MCP servers in a session. Refusals are JSON-RPC errors: -32700 for a line that is not JSON, -32600 for a message that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request, -32601 for a method this agent does not implement, and -32602 for invalid parameters, including a prompt that is not valid TOML ( BRIEF_INVALID ) or a kind this build cannot start. An unexpected failure is -32603 with the message internal error ; only the exception's class name is written to stderr, because a message can carry a connection string. A refusal with no JSON-RPC code of its own, such as a brief above EI_MAX_RUN_BUDGET_MICRO_USD , is also -32603 , with the refusal's own message. Webhooks ¶ Deliveries are POST requests with a JSON body {"id", "type", "data"} (compact, sorted keys) and these headers: Header Value X-Engineering-Influence-Signature v1= + hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>." + raw body) X-Engineering-Influence-Timestamp Unix seconds X-Engineering-Influence-Event / -Event-Id event name and id X-Request-ID , traceparent present when the event has a correlation id A receiver must, in order: check the signature over the raw bytes , check the timestamp is within 300 seconds, and refuse a signature it has already seen. Answer 2xx to acknowledge; anything else is retried and, after max_attempts (default 5), dead-lettered with an alert. Destinations must be public https URLs; loopback, private ranges and cloud metadata addresses are refused. examples/webhooks/receiver.py is a stdlib receiver and examples/webhooks/send_event.py sends it valid, replayed, tampered and stale deliveries. No service emits webhooks yet ; the sender reproduces the request the platform will make so you can build a receiver now.

docs.text: BLUF: Every interface drives the same thing, a book run that ends in a KDP-ready package, so learn one and you know them all. To write one book, use the CLI ( ei book create ). To serve many, run the stack and call it over REST, the SDK, MCP or the Agent Client Protocol. This page is the contract for each: requests, replies, flags, exit codes and the error codes a caller meets most. Every interface starts or drives the same thing: an autonomous book-writing run that ends in a KDP-ready package ( details ). Six interfaces sit over the same controller layer, so they accept the same request and return the same result. Pick by who is calling. Interface Process Authenticated Reaches the stack REST API ei serve api API key yes Python SDK your code API key yes (it calls the REST API) MCP server stdio child process no (local only) yes with ei serve mcp ; the example server is in-memory CLI ei no (local only) serve , run and book yes; pipeline start no Agent Client Protocol ei acp (stdio) no (local only) yes Webhooks outbound HTTPS HMAC signature yes
docs.title: Interfaces reference

docs.text: Daniel: Six ways in. REST, an SDK, MCP, a CLI, ACP, webhooks. Do I have to learn six products? Professor Feynman: Think of a bank. You can walk to the counter, use the machine outside, or phone. How many banks is that? Daniel: One. The same account, the same rules, whichever way I ask. Professor Feynman: Same here. Each interface is a window; behind all of them is one counter, the controller layer. A window translates your request and hands it over. The rules about runs and money live behind the counter. A window may be stricter, never looser: the MCP window caps a run at five dollars and cannot grant more budget unless you allow it. Daniel: So if the API refuses a budget above the operator's limit, the MCP tool refuses it too. Professor Feynman: For the same reason, though not in the same words. REST gives you a code, BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT . MCP and ACP give you the message. Now the limit of the picture: not every window is open to the street. The REST API checks a key. The CLI, the MCP server and ACP check nothing, because they are meant to run on your own machine, so they must never be put on a network. Daniel: Then I pick the window by who is calling, and I read one set of rules. I will start at the table below.
docs.title: One counter, several windows

docs.text: Every start request is a project : Field Type Rules slug string required, at least 1 character title string required, at least 1 character postulates list of strings required, at least 1: the claims the pipeline must stay within stages list of strings required, at least 1, from thesis , book , novel , screenplay , hub , spokes , distribution , publish The result is {"job_id": "<id>", "project_slug": "<slug>"} : the job queued for the first stage. The worker runs the stages in the order given. A book run starts from a brief instead ( POST /v1/runs , ei run create , the SDK and MCP create_run , and ei book create , which builds one from its flags). Any key not in this table is refused: Field Rules schema_version 1 , the default kind required: nonfiction or novel idea required, not blank budget_micro_usd required: a whole number above 0, in millionths of a dollar title_hint , audience optional, not blank target_words optional, above 0 trim_size optional: 5x8 , 5.5x8.5 or 6x9 language default en inputs at most 8 of {name, text, origin} ; origin is pasted (the default) or file ; names unique; 200,000 characters in all violence novels only: none , mild , moderate or graphic heat novels only: none , sweet , steamy or explicit
docs.title: The request

docs.text: Run it with ei serve api (see CONFIGURATION.md ); the compose stack publishes it on 127.0.0.1:8000 . Method and path Auth Purpose POST /v1/pipelines key Start a pipeline. Body: a project. 200 with the result. GET /v1/runs key Every saved run, as run summaries (the artifact list is empty here; GET /v1/runs/{run_id} lists a run's artifacts). 200 . Present only when the API is wired with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/resume key Un-park a parked run and queue its current stage. 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 finished. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel key Stop a run for good. 200 with the run; 404 unknown. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/grant key Give a run more budget and continue it. Body {"micro_usd": N} or none: a run waiting for consent gets exactly the amount it asked for (a different amount is 409 ); a parked run needs micro_usd . 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 not waiting or parked, or changed meanwhile. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/deny key Refuse a run's request for more budget; the run parks and nothing is queued. 200 with the run; 404 unknown; 409 not waiting for consent. Present only with run management. POST /v1/runs key Start a book run from a brief (the brief contract v1, the same body ei run create reads as TOML). 201 with the new run, pending at its first stage; 422 when the body is not a brief or the kind is not one this build can start. Present only when the API is wired with run creation. GET /v1/runs/{run_id} key A book run: status, stage, plan, budget in micro-dollars, issues and the names of its artifacts. 200 with a RunSummaryV1 . GET /v1/runs/{run_id}/artifacts/{name} key One stored artifact, byte for byte, as application/octet-stream with nosniff and no-store . Names may contain / . GET /health/live none {"status":"alive"} while the process runs. GET /health/ready none 200 {"status":"ready"} or 503 {"status":"unavailable"} . GET /metrics key Prometheus text format. GET /docs , /openapi.json none FastAPI's generated schema for this build. Authentication. Send Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-API-Key: <key> . Keys come from EI_API_KEYS . There is no unauthenticated mode. Correlation. Send X-Request-ID (8 to 64 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ - ) or a W3C traceparent ; otherwise one is generated. It is echoed in the X-Request-ID response header, copied into the queued job, restored by the worker and sent on outbound webhooks. Errors. Application errors are {"code", "message", "retryable"} : Status code Meaning Retry? 401 UNAUTHORIZED Missing or wrong key no 429 RATE_LIMITED Per-address or per-key budget spent yes, with backoff 404 RUN_NOT_FOUND No run has that id no 404 ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND The run has no such artifact; a name that could never be stored (absolute, .. , backslash) gets the same answer no 422 n/a Body failed validation (FastAPI's detail list) no, fix the body 409 RUN_FINISHED The run is completed, failed or cancelled, so it cannot be resumed or cancelled no 409 RUN_CHANGED The run changed while it was being answered yes 409 CONSENT_NOT_PENDING A grant or a denial for a run that is not waiting for one no 422 BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT The budget asked for is above the operator's limit for one run no, ask for less 422 OUTSTANDING_BUDGET_EXCEEDED All unfinished runs together would hold more unspent budget than the operator allows later, when runs finish 422 RUN_KIND_UNSUPPORTED This build cannot start that kind of book no 503 SECRET_MISSING A required secret is not configured after fixing configuration These are the codes a caller of the API meets most. Every code the package can raise is frozen in tests/contracts/snapshots/error_codes.json ; most of the rest stop a process at start and are described beside the setting they concern in CONFIGURATION.md . Python with requests : import os, requests base, key = os.environ["EI_BASE_URL"], os.environ["EI_API_KEY"] reply = requests.post( f"{base}/v1/pipelines", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {key}"}, json={ "slug": "sample-essay", "title": "A Sample Essay", "postulates": ["Claims must be supported by evidence."], "stages": ["thesis"], }, timeout=10, ) reply.raise_for_status() print(reply.json()) # {'job_id': '…', 'project_slug': 'sample-essay'} Full scripts: examples/api/start_pipeline.py , examples/api/run.sh .
docs.title: REST API

docs.text: packages/engineering-influence-sdk is a thin typed wrapper over httpx for the operations the API has: starting a pipeline, creating a book run from a brief ( create_run ), and listing, resuming and cancelling runs ( list_runs , resume_run , cancel_run ), answering a run's request for more budget ( grant_run , deny_run ), and reading a run ( get_run ) and the files it stored ( get_artifact , as bytes). It ships in this repository and in each release. from engineering_influence_sdk import EngineeringInfluenceClient client = EngineeringInfluenceClient("http://127.0.0.1:8000", api_key) started = client.start_pipeline( "sample-essay", "A Sample Essay", ("Claims must be supported by evidence.",), ("thesis", "book") ) run = client.create_run( { "schema_version": 1, "kind": "nonfiction", "idea": "Windowsill herbs", "budget_micro_usd": 5000000, } ) status = client.get_run(run["run_id"]) # status, stage, budget and the names of its artifacts pdf = client.get_artifact(run["run_id"], "book/my-book.pdf") # bytes, once the run has built it client.close() AsyncEngineeringInfluenceClient has the same signature with await (and await client.close() ). Any non-2xx answer raises httpx.HTTPStatusError ; the API's error document is in error.response . Scripts: examples/sdk/ .
docs.title: Python SDK

docs.text: ei serve mcp runs the stack's MCP server over stdio, for an MCP host (Claude Desktop, an agent runtime) to start as a child process. It needs EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL like the API (and a migrated database: ei db upgrade ), offers the same runs the REST API does, and needs no API key because the host that starts it already holds the stack's credentials. Standard output carries the protocol, so logs (JSON) go to standard error only. A host entry looks like: {"mcpServers": {"engineering-influence": {"command": "ei", "args": ["serve", "mcp"], "env": {"EI_DATABASE_URL": "postgresql+psycopg://...", "EI_RABBITMQ_URL": "amqp://..."}}}} The server does not offer grant_run or deny_run unless the operator sets EI_MCP_ALLOW_SPEND=1 . Granting a run budget is the person's decision, and an agent that could raise its own run's cap would have no cap. Without the setting an agent can start a run, watch it, resume or cancel it and read what it made; a run that needs more budget shows as awaiting_consent in get_run , and the person answers it with ei run grant . A run an agent starts is held to EI_MCP_MAX_RUN_BUDGET_MICRO_USD (default 5,000,000, five dollars): create_run refuses a brief with a bigger budget_micro_usd ( BUDGET_ABOVE_LIMIT ), so an agent cannot open a run with a cap of its own choosing. That bounds one run, not how many runs an agent starts . For that, set the stack-wide ceilings below ( EI_MAX_OUTSTANDING_BUDGET_MICRO_USD ), which hold every way into the stack, MCP included. McpApplication(controller).build() returns an MCPServer (from the official mcp 2.x SDK) with one tool when built bare, and the rest when it is given the services ( grant_run and deny_run only with allow_spend=True ): Tool Arguments Returns start_pipeline slug , title , postulates (list), stages (list) {"job_id", "project_slug"} list_runs none every saved run as run summaries (present only with run management) resume_run run_id the run after un-parking it (present only with run management) cancel_run run_id the run after cancelling it (present only with run management) get_run run_id a run's RunSummaryV1 : status, stage, budget and the names of its stored artifacts (present only when the server is built with a run reader) read_artifact run_id , name (such as book/my-book.pdf ) {name, bytes, encoding, content} : the text when the file is UTF-8, base64 when it is not. A file over 1 MiB is refused ( ARTIFACT_TOO_LARGE ) and the message names the GET /v1/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name} address that downloads any size (present with get_run ) create_run brief (an object: the brief contract v1) the new run as a RunSummaryV1 , pending at its first stage. Present only when the server is built with a run creator grant_run run_id , optional micro_usd the run after allowing it more budget. Present only with allow_spend=True ( ei serve mcp sets it from EI_MCP_ALLOW_SPEND ) deny_run run_id the run after refusing it more budget; it parks. Present only with allow_spend=True examples/mcp/server.py is the bare server over in-memory adapters, for trying the tool shapes without a stack, and examples/mcp/client.py is a client that spawns it, lists the tools and calls one. The server is a local process: it is not authenticated, so do not expose it on a network.

The run is saved pending with the brief's cap as its budget and its first stage is queued for the worker; a file that is not a brief, or a kind this build cannot start, is refused on one line and nothing is saved. Needs the database and the broker, like resume . 0 ; 1 a file that cannot be read or is not a brief, or a kind this build cannot start; 2 setup trouble, or a budget an operator ceiling refuses ei run runs Lists every saved run, one line each: its id, status and current stage. Needs only the database. 0 ; 2 setup trouble ei run resume RUN_ID Moves a parked run back to running and queues its current stage; on a run that is already running it only queues the stage again, which repairs a resume that died half-way. Reads EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL . 0 ; 1 unknown run, finished run or a run that kept changing; 2 setup trouble ei run cancel RUN_ID Stops a run for good; cancelling twice is fine, and a completed or failed run is refused. A run waiting for consent gets exactly the amount it asked for (passing another amount is refused); a parked run needs --micro-usd and gets exactly that. The stage is queued. Needs EI_DATABASE_URL and EI_RABBITMQ_URL . 0 ; 1 the run is not waiting for consent or parked, or it changed while being answered; 2 setup trouble, or a grant an operator ceiling refuses ei run deny RUN_ID Refuses a run's request for more budget. The run parks, and nothing is queued; it can be granted more later. Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . same ei run export RUN_ID DIRECTORY Writes what a run produced to a new or empty folder: the book as a project at the top ( books/<slug>.toml and src/chapter_NN.md , as the book commands expect) and every other artifact under run/ (the stage outputs and the audit/ reports). It reads the run and changes nothing in it. Nothing is overwritten, and either every file is written or none is. A folder that holds anything is refused, as is a run that has stored nothing. Needs only EI_DATABASE_URL . 0 ; 1 unknown run, a run with nothing stored, or a folder that is not empty; 2 setup trouble ei book create --kind KIND IDEA --budget-usd N --out DIR --profile FILE Makes a whole book from an idea, in this process, with nobody in the loop. It runs every stage of the plan for the kind (brief to build; see BOOKS_AND_KDP.md ) with the models and search the environment names ( EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR and its settings, as for a worker), then writes the book to --out (a new or empty folder): the project at the top ( books/ , src/ ) and every artifact under run/ , so the finished PDF, EPUB, covers, listing and manifest are in run/book/ , the readiness reports in run/build/ , and run/quality-report.json says how it came out. --budget-usd has no default, and --profile (or EI_AUTHOR_PROFILE ) is required, because the author's details are needed to typeset the book: both are checked before anything is spent . Before anything is spent it says what the book is expected to cost with the priced model ( estimate: about 6.00 USD for the whole book (4.00 before editing), against a budget of 5.00: tight ) and grades the budget: short (below what the essential stages are expected to cost: refused, with the budget that would do, unless --ignore-estimate ), tight (may stop to ask for more), lean (an editing pass that runs out of money is skipped) or ample . With the free local model the estimate is still printed, from a price of zero; with the offline placeholder there is no estimate. Optional: --title , --audience , --target-words , --trim-size , --ignore-estimate , and --strict-release (fails the build on any release warning; needs [pricing] in the profile). The run is kept in a SQLite file in OUT.state/ ( --state-dir to move it), so a process that dies loses nothing that was paid for: --resume continues it, and a model call already made is replayed, not paid for again. When the run asks for more budget it stops and writes nothing; --resume --approve-spend grants exactly what it asked for. A failed run is final, but what it made is still written to --out . 0 the book is written; 1 the run failed or a needed extra is missing; 2 the command could not start (a missing idea, kind, budget or profile, a bad profile, a folder that already holds a run, or a budget below the estimate without --ignore-estimate ); 3 the run stopped to ask for budget, or parked because the provider is at capacity ei book … Audit, build and publish books (needs the publishing extra and, for PDFs, a TeX toolchain). With no SLUG a subcommand works on every configured book. --dpi defaults to 90, and below 36 is refused (exit 2 ). package SLUG writes the KDP release bundle ( build/SLUG/release/kdp , see BOOKS_AND_KDP.md ) and refuses a failing release. Reads engineering-influence.toml in --root . 0 ok; 1 a build or audit failure; 2 bad arguments ei evaluate --out DIR --budget-usd N --judge-budget-usd N Spends real money. Makes every book of the evaluation set ( evaluation/set.toml ) with the stack's own pipeline, has the judge model ( EI_EVAL_JUDGE_PROFILE ) score each finished book on the rubric ( evaluation/rubric.toml ), and checks the release against the 1.0 bar: every book finished, every dimension's mean at least 3.5, none fallen by more than 0.2 from --baseline , and the cost estimate within 30% of what was spent. Refuses to start unless EI_ALLOW_PAID=1 . --budget-usd is the most each book may spend and --judge-budget-usd the most the judge may spend in all; neither has a default. --out must be a new or empty folder; evaluation.json is written there beside the books, and is the next release's baseline. See EVALUATION.md . 0 the release meets the bar; 1 it does not (each reason is printed) or a needed extra is missing; 2 the command could not run (not paid for, a bad budget, a folder that is not empty, a bad rubric or set, no judge named, or a judge that failed) ei tools add NAME -- COMMAND … Runs an MCP server once, under limits and with a bare environment, and records what it is in the tool lock: its files' hashes, the name and version it reported and a hash of its tools. Options go before NAME . Refuses a launcher ( npx , uvx , docker , …) and a relative script path before anything is run. See TOOL_LOCK.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools add --url URL NAME Contacts a remote MCP server once and records its address, the name and version it reported and a hash of its tools. Only https to a public address is allowed; the token, if any, is the variable named by --bearer-env . The server's code is not locked, only what it advertises. See TOOL_LOCK.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools list Shows the locked servers. Starts nothing. 0 ; 2 an unusable lock ei tools verify [NAME …] Runs each locked server (a server whose files changed is not started) and compares it with the lock. 0 all match; 1 one does not; 2 setup trouble or an unknown name ei tools grant NAME STAGE TOOL … Lets a stage call some of a locked server's tools: edits the lock, runs nothing. The tools must be ones the lock lists; no wildcards. A stage with no grant gets none. 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei tools revoke NAME STAGE [TOOL …] Takes tools back from a stage, or all of them if none are named. A stage with no grant is an error. same ei skills add FILE Reads a skill file once, checks it strictly (no key but name , version , description and [parts] ; no invisible or control characters) and records the SHA-256 of its bytes in the skill lock, keeping a copy in skills/ beside it. Enables nothing ; prints each part so you can read what will be added to prompts. --replace locks it again and clears its stages. Starts nothing. See SKILLS.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal or an unusable lock ei skills import SOURCE … Turns a SKILL.md (a --- block of key: value lines, then markdown) into a skill file ( --out ) and prints what it kept and set aside, to be reviewed and then added. It does not touch the lock. See SKILLS.md . 0 ; 2 an unreadable source or a bad option ei skills enable NAME STAGE Lets a stage's prompt carry a skill: checks the file against its hash and refuses a stage the skill has no text for. At most four skills per stage. same ei skills disable NAME STAGE Stops a stage carrying a skill. same ei skills remove NAME Unlocks a skill and deletes its copy. same ei skills list Shows the locked skills with their short hash and stages. Reads no skill file. 0 ; 2 an unusable lock ei skills verify Re-hashes every locked skill, enabled or not, against the lock. 0 all match; 1 one does not; 2 setup trouble ei plugins show FILE Reads a plugin file and says what installing it would do: its skills (with their text), and the ei tools add command for each server. Changes nothing. See PLUGINS.md . 0 ; 2 on a refusal ei plugins import FOLDER Turns a plugin folder written for Claude Code into a bundle file ( --out ), to be shown and then added. It does not touch the lock. See PLUGINS.md . 0 ; 2 an unreadable folder or a bad option ei plugins add FILE Locks the bundle's skills (each enabled for no stage), keeps a copy of the bundle, and records its SHA-256 in the plugin lock. Starts nothing, contacts nothing, grants nothing: the commands for its servers are printed for you to review and run. docs.text: ei acp speaks the Agent Client Protocol, version 1 of the stable specification, so an editor or agent client can start book runs the way ei run create does. Only the parts below are implemented; anything else is refused with ACP_METHOD_NOT_FOUND . initialize agrees version 1, reports loadSession: true and no authentication methods. session/load takes a sessionId this agent stored, and an absolute cwd . It re-attaches the session, so a client can reconnect to a new ei acp process. It sends one session/update notice with the run's current state (if the session has a run), then replies with no result. A run that has finished is replayed but not followed. session/new takes an absolute cwd and returns a sessionId . mcpServers must be empty: this agent does not connect MCP servers yet. session/prompt takes text content blocks, joined by newlines and read as a brief in TOML, the same contract ei run create reads. The first prompt of a session starts its run, a second prompt in the same session is refused, and the turn ends with stopReason: end_turn once the run is saved and its first stage queued. The stages themselves run in the worker, not in the session. Before the turn ends the agent sends one session/update notice naming the run and its stage. session/cancel is a notification. It stops the session's run and gets no reply. Sessions are stored in the database beside the runs, so any ei acp process can load one. A run outlives its session, so ei run status RUN_ID and ei run cancel RUN_ID still work after the client disconnects. The session store needs migration 0002 : run ei db upgrade first. While a session is open, the agent follows its run. Every second it reads the run's saved state, and it sends a session/update notice when the status or the stage changes, once per change. A finished run (completed, failed or cancelled) is reported once and then no longer followed; a parked run is still followed, because it can be resumed. A notice is written between replies and never inside one. A failed read is one line on stderr, and the following goes on. A run that would spend past its cap does not fail: its next model call is refused before it spends, and the run stops in awaiting_consent with the amount the call needs. An open session is asked, with a session/request_permission request that offers grant (allow exactly that amount) and deny (the run parks). The answer decides the run; a cancelled answer leaves it waiting. The same decision is available from the command line with ei run grant and ei run deny for any run, including one with no open session. A parked run waiting for no decision continues with ei run grant RUN_ID --micro-usd N . Not yet implemented: MCP servers in a session. Refusals are JSON-RPC errors: -32700 for a line that is not JSON, -32600 for a message that is not a JSON-RPC 2.0 request, -32601 for a method this agent does not implement, and -32602 for invalid parameters, including a prompt that is not valid TOML ( BRIEF_INVALID ) or a kind this build cannot start. An unexpected failure is -32603 with the message internal error ; only the exception's class name is written to stderr, because a message can carry a connection string. A refusal with no JSON-RPC code of its own, such as a brief above EI_MAX_RUN_BUDGET_MICRO_USD , is also -32603 , with the refusal's own message.
docs.title: Agent Client Protocol

docs.text: Deliveries are POST requests with a JSON body {"id", "type", "data"} (compact, sorted keys) and these headers: Header Value X-Engineering-Influence-Signature v1= + hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, "<timestamp>." + raw body) X-Engineering-Influence-Timestamp Unix seconds X-Engineering-Influence-Event / -Event-Id event name and id X-Request-ID , traceparent present when the event has a correlation id A receiver must, in order: check the signature over the raw bytes , check the timestamp is within 300 seconds, and refuse a signature it has already seen. Answer 2xx to acknowledge; anything else is retried and, after max_attempts (default 5), dead-lettered with an alert. Destinations must be public https URLs; loopback, private ranges and cloud metadata addresses are refused. examples/webhooks/receiver.py is a stdlib receiver and examples/webhooks/send_event.py sends it valid, replayed, tampered and stale deliveries. No service emits webhooks yet ; the sender reproduces the request the platform will make so you can build a receiver now.
docs.title: Webhooks

docs.text: Running a small book against a real model ¶ BLUF: This is the smallest paid run that proves the whole chain against a real model: one short non-fiction book, in one process, with a spending cap you set first. It never runs by default and will not start unless the environment says you mean to spend. Until someone runs it, nothing in the writing pipeline has ever talked to a live model. Until this has been done, nothing in the writing pipeline has ever talked to a live model . Everything is tested against scripted servers and fakes. This page is how you find out whether the prompts, the editing passes and the whole chain work with a real one, and what it costs, with a limit you set in advance. The test drives the whole non-fiction plan (brief, positioning, research, outline, metadata, draft, three editing passes, assemble, audit, build) in one process, with no database, queue or worker. It writes every artifact and a report to a folder you can read. It is a paid test: it never runs by default, and it will not start unless you say in the environment that you mean to spend. What a passing test does not prove ¶ Daniel: Ten thousand tests pass. Is that not proof the writing works? Professor Feynman: A flight simulator can pass every drill. What has never happened in it? Daniel: Real weather. Real air. Professor Feynman: Every test here flies against a scripted model that answers exactly as the test wrote. That proves the machinery: the stages, the budget, the resume. It cannot prove that a real model follows these prompts, or what a book really costs. Daniel: So this test is the first real flight. Why is it so hedged about? Professor Feynman: Because it spends your money. You set the cap before it starts, it refuses to run without an explicit yes in the environment, and it writes down what it spent. And mind the limit even of a real flight: one short book on one model on one day. A pass means the chain holds together, not that the books are good. Daniel: Scripted tests prove the machine, this proves the chain, and neither proves quality. That is what the evaluation is for. What it spends, and what stops it ¶ A cap you must set. EI_SMOKE_BUDGET_MICRO_USD is the most the run may spend, in millionths of a dollar ( 3000000 is three dollars). There is no default, on purpose; a run without one does not start. A reservation before every call. Each call reserves its worst case (its full output allowance at the model's price) against the cap, and a call that would pass the cap is refused before it is made. The run then stops at that stage and says so. So the cap is a ceiling on what is spent, and a cap smaller than a few worst-case calls stops the run early. The size of the book. EI_SMOKE_TARGET_WORDS (default 1,200) shapes the brief, and the outline decides how many chapters there are. Each chapter costs about five calls: a draft, a summary and three edits. A short target keeps it small, but the number of chapters is the model's choice, so the cap is what actually bounds the cost. A made-up author. The run always uses a fictional author profile. It never reads yours. What you need ¶ A model profile and a price catalog for the model you want to test ( MODEL_PROFILES.md , MODEL_CATALOG.md ), and the key in the environment variable the profile names. Check them first, which sends nothing: ei doctor --models . A web search for the research stage: EI_SEARXNG_URL (a SearXNG instance) or BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY ( CONFIGURATION.md , RESEARCH.md ). Without one the run stops at start with a clear message, before any call. Check that it answers first, which sends one search per provider and asks no model anything: ei doctor --search . A dev install with the extras the audit and the runtime need: uv sync --extra runtime --extra publishing . The TeX toolchain ( latexmk , lualatex , tex4ebook , zip , and pdftoppm or mutool ; epubcheck is optional unless the release is strict; ei doctor --ready checks them all; WORKER_IMAGE.md ) for the last stage, build , which turns the run's book into a PDF, an EPUB and the KDP bundle. Without it every earlier stage still runs and is reported, and build fails naming the missing tool. Run it ¶ EI_ALLOW_PAID=1 \ EI_SMOKE_PROFILE=hosted \ EI_MODEL_PROFILES=profiles.toml \ EI_MODEL_CATALOG=catalog.toml \ EI_SMOKE_BUDGET_MICRO_USD=3000000 \ EI_SMOKE_OUT=./smoke-out \ uv run pytest -m paid tests/paid Variable EI_ALLOW_PAID must be exactly 1 , or the test fails before it starts EI_SMOKE_PROFILE the name of the profile to use EI_MODEL_PROFILES , EI_MODEL_CATALOG the two files EI_SMOKE_BUDGET_MICRO_USD the hard cap, required EI_SMOKE_TARGET_WORDS optional, default 1,200 EI_SMOKE_IDEA optional; the book's idea, default a short one about windowsill herbs EI_SMOKE_OUT optional; a folder that does not exist or is empty. Default: a temporary folder, printed at the end It prints each stage with its outcome, its cost and its time, then the folder. The folder is written even when the run fails , so you can see how far it got. Novels are not in this test yet ¶ The test above drives the non-fiction plan only. A novel run is brief, story bible, beats, outline, metadata, draft, assemble, audit and build, with no editing passes (see NOVELS.md ). Pointing EI_SMOKE_IDEA at a novel would not make the test write a novel: the smoke harness always builds a non-fiction brief and plan. So there is no paid novel check yet. A novel live check needs the paid harness to take a novel brief (the rehearsal driver already runs a novel plan). Until then, a novel has only ever been run against scripted servers, and its first real-model run will be a manual one with ei doctor --local and the prompts. What to read afterwards ¶ In the folder: smoke-report.json : the status, the spend against the cap, and each stage's outcome, attempts, cost and seconds. outline.md , metadata.md , chapter_NN.md , copy_NN.md : what each stage wrote. Read a draft chapter next to its structure_NN , lines_NN and copy_NN versions to judge whether the editing passes helped. The report's revision-unchanged issues name chapters an edit changed nothing in or whose edit was not kept. audit.md and audit/ : the book's own audit. A made-up author passes it with warnings about prices. manuscript/ : the book as a project ( books/<slug>.toml , src/chapter_NN.md ). book/ : the built book: <slug>.pdf , <slug>.epub , the covers, listing.md and MANIFEST.json . build/ holds the readiness reports and the tool logs, quality-report.json the status with a checksum for every file, and build.md a summary. What a pass does and does not show ¶ A pass shows that the chain works with a real provider (the adapter, token counting, cost reservation, refusals, every executor, the audit) and what it costs. It does not show that the prose is good or that the facts are right: there is no claim checking yet, and the only automatic judgment of an edit is its length. Read the chapters yourself. A failure is information. The usual ones: a stage whose answer is not in the format a program reads (the outline or the listing), a model whose window is too small for a chapter ( STAGE_MODEL_TOO_SMALL ), or a cap that was too small. Without spending ¶ tests/unit/test_smoke_run.py runs the same driver against a scripted local server. It is the free rehearsal, and it runs in the normal suite. It proves the chain, the budget stop, the retry and the folder, and says nothing about a real model's answers.

docs.text: The free local model ¶ BLUF: By default the book is written by gpt-oss:20b , an open-source model running on your own machine through Ollama. It costs nothing per word and needs no key, and your prompts and manuscript stay on the machine (the research stage still sends search queries out and fetches public pages). It uses about 13 GB of memory when loaded and needs a context of 32,768 tokens; ei doctor --local checks the server, the model, one tiny answer and the context it really loaded. With nothing configured, a run is written by an open-source model on your own machine. It costs nothing per token and needs no key. The model itself sends nothing off the machine; the research stage's search and page fetches do. Model gpt-oss:20b , Apache 2.0, about 13 GB Server Ollama at http://127.0.0.1:11434 Search for research a SearXNG at http://127.0.0.1:8888 (the compose example in examples/searxng ) Context 32,768 tokens, which the server must really offer Why the context size is checked ¶ Daniel: The model is pulled and it answers. Why does the doctor also fuss about a number called context? Professor Feynman: How much of a long letter can you keep in your head while you write the reply? Daniel: Most of it. If it were fifty pages I would lose the start. Professor Feynman: The context is how much the model can hold at once: its instructions, the outline, what came before. This project packs a prompt to fit 32,768 tokens. If the server quietly offers fewer, it does not complain. It cuts the prompt short. Daniel: And whatever was cut might be the instructions, or the outline. Professor Feynman: You would not know which. You would get a chapter that reads well and ignores part of what it was given, and you would blame the model. So the doctor asks the server what it really loaded. The picture is imperfect: you know when you have lost the start of a letter. The model does not. Daniel: So a wrong context fails silently, and the check is the only way I would find out. I will run it before the first book. Set it up ¶ ollama pull gpt-oss:20b OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32768 ollama serve The second line matters. Ollama's own default context is much smaller, and a prompt is assembled to fit the 32,768 tokens this project assumes, so a server that quietly offers less would cut a prompt short. Set the variable wherever you start Ollama (the macOS app reads it from launchctl setenv OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH 32768 ), then run ei doctor --local to confirm. A model on a laptop with 24 GB of memory used about 13 GB loaded. Use another model or server ¶ EI_LOCAL_MODEL names another model and EI_LOCAL_URL another server that speaks the OpenAI chat shape (Ollama, llama.cpp's llama-server , vLLM, LM Studio). Both are trimmed, and blank means the default. A model other than the default is yours to vet: the cost is zero by construction, but the 32,768 window and the low reasoning effort are still what a run assumes. A model you pay for is EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR=model with your own profile and price catalog ( MODEL_PROFILES.md , MODEL_CATALOG.md ); EI_STAGE_EXECUTOR=deterministic calls no model at all. Why this model ¶ It was picked by running the four candidates already installed on the author's 24 GB Apple Silicon laptop over three book-copy tasks (a non-fiction section, a line edit, a fiction scene), each told to use no em or en dashes and none of six filler words. gpt-oss:20b kept to the instruction on every task; qwen3:14b (also Apache 2.0) used dashes in two of three. That is a small test of one person's machine on one afternoon, run while the machine was busy, so its speeds (12 to 20 tokens a second) are not a benchmark, and it says nothing about quality beyond rule-following. Two of the other candidates, gemma4:26b and llama3.1:8b , did not finish the comparison and are not ranked. The licence matters too: Apache 2.0 is open source, while Gemma's terms and the Llama community licence are open-weight but not. Reasoning ¶ gpt-oss thinks before it answers, and the thinking counts against a stage's token cap. With the cap at 1,200 tokens a line edit came back empty, because the thinking used all of it. The default profile therefore sends reasoning_effort: low , which answered the same task in 40 tokens. If you point at a reasoning model of your own, set reasoning_effort in its profile for the same reason. Check it: ei doctor --local ¶ ei doctor --local It makes four checks and stops at the first thing that makes the rest pointless: Check Passes when If it fails server something answers at EI_LOCAL_URL install and start Ollama, or set EI_LOCAL_URL model the model is pulled ollama pull <model> answers one tiny real completion comes back non-empty the model spent its whole cap before writing a word context the loaded context is at least 32,768 tokens set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH and restart Ollama In more detail: server : something answers at EI_LOCAL_URL . Ollama is recognised by /api/tags ; another server that speaks the chat shape ( llama-server , vLLM, LM Studio) passes with a note; the model and context checks are skipped and answers still runs. model : the model is pulled; if not, it names ollama pull <model> . answers : one tiny real completion, free and on this machine. An empty reply fails, because a reasoning model can spend its whole cap before it writes a word. context : the context length Ollama loaded the model with is at least the 32,768 a prompt is assembled to fit. If not, it names OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH . Ollama would otherwise cut a prompt short without saying so. Exit 0 when all held, 1 when one failed, 2 when a setting cannot be used. The first call loads the model into memory, so it can take a minute. It was run once against the author's Ollama, which loaded the model with a 131,072 context. What is not checked yet ¶ Nothing here has been run through a whole book. The first run on a real topic will show whether a 20-billion parameter model holds a chapter together, and the checks that read a draft (the dash and filler scans, the continuity checker for novels) catch some of what it gets wrong, not all.
